result.finding: Assessed 16 CWE rules in Code Quality: 3 FOUND, 13 NOT_FOUND
evidence: All 16 code-quality rules assessed against complete production source, templates/JavaScript, properties, and container/bootstrap scripts; not a diff review.

CWE-130/CWE-456/CWE-457 NOT_FOUND: no application-defined message-length parser, uninitialized Java local, or critical missing state initializer identified. UploadResult false defaults are deliberate; optional dimensions are explicitly null and template-guarded.
CWE-477 NOT_FOUND: no confirmed obsolete function against the actual resolved Spring 5.3 / Security 5.7 API baseline. APIs deprecated only in later framework releases were not mislabeled.
CWE-570/CWE-571/CWE-783 NOT_FOUND: branches and arithmetic were reviewed without a confirmed always-constant security decision or precedence error.

CWE-681/CWE-682 NOT_FOUND: PhotoServiceImpl.java:138 widens each dimension to long before multiplication; the pixel-count check does not overflow int. MathUtil.java:14-20 has ordinary signed-int GCD behavior and no security-sensitive call sites.

CWE-772/CWE-775 NOT_FOUND: PhotoServiceImpl.java:130-149 closes ImageInputStream and disposes ImageReader in finally; azure-setup.ps1:19-20 disposes its cryptographic RNG. JPA/JDBC lifecycle is framework-managed.
CWE-835 NOT_FOUND: MathUtil.java:15-19 reduces the remainder until b is zero; JavaScript loops traverse finite arrays. No unreachable exit established.
CWE-1057 NOT_FOUND: controllers use PhotoService and runtime persistence is centralized through PhotoRepository; operator bootstrap SQL is not a bypass of the request data-manager layer.
No load test, database recreation, or runtime exploit was executed. Resource-exhaustion consequences depend on workload, dataset, and deployment limits.

values.name: Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency
values.description: The product parses a formatted message or structure, but it does not handle or incorrectly handles a length field that is inconsistent with the actual length of the associated data.

values.name: Missing Initialization of a Variable
values.description: The product does not initialize critical variables, which causes the execution environment to use unexpected values.

values.name: Use of Uninitialized Variable
values.description: The code uses a variable that has not been initialized, leading to unpredictable or unintended results.

values.name: Use of Obsolete Function
values.description: The code uses deprecated or obsolete functions, which suggests that the code has not been actively reviewed or maintained.

values.name: Expression is Always False
values.description: The product contains an expression that will always evaluate to false.

values.name: Expression is Always True
values.description: The product contains an expression that will always evaluate to true.

values.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition

evidence.explanation: HomeController.uploadPhotos checks only null/empty at 62-66, then iterates the entire attacker-supplied multipart files list at 68-90, performing upload processing and accumulating per-file results. The configured app.file-upload.max-files-per-upload=10 is never injected or enforced anywhere in production code. Authenticated callers can cause processing of substantially more files than the intended ten, including many tiny/empty files and associated result objects. The 50MB multipart byte limit at application.properties:25 bounds bytes, not the application file-count loop; actual transport/container limits still apply. This is a concrete missing application count check, not a claim of an infinite loop.

values.description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

values.name: Improper Initialization

evidence.explanation: Both the default and Docker runtime profiles configure spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=create. Hibernate recreates the mapped PHOTOS schema on application startup, so existing photo records/BLOBs are discarded rather than preserved across restarts. This destructive startup initialization conflicts with the persistent Oracle data volume configured in docker-compose.yml:13 and the application persistent photo-storage role. No cloud runtime override was inspected; the finding concerns checked-in effective defaults.

values.description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.

values.name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
values.description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.

values.name: Incorrect Calculation
values.description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.

values.name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
values.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

values.name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
values.description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

values.name: Operator Precedence Logic Error
values.description: The product uses an expression in which operator precedence causes incorrect logic to be used.

values.name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

evidence.explanation: Public GET / calls HomeController.index -> PhotoServiceImpl.getAllPhotos -> PhotoRepository.findAllOrderByUploadedAtDesc, whose unbounded query selects PHOTO_DATA for every row (repository lines 22-27). Photo.photoData is a byte[] @Lob with default eager fetching (model lines 39-41), so a gallery request materializes all uploaded BLOB bytes instead of bounded metadata. There is a 10MB per-file limit but no aggregate record/byte bound. A sufficiently large existing album can exceed the configured 512MB heap (Dockerfile:28), and anonymous requests can repeatedly trigger this allocation. Uploading new records requires authentication; this is dataset-dependent public memory-exhaustion exposure, not an arbitrary-size unauthenticated single-upload allocation.

values.description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.

values.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
values.description: The product contains an iteration or loop with an exit condition that cannot be reached, i.e., an infinite loop.

values.name: Data Access Operations Outside of Expected Data Manager Component
values.description: The product uses a dedicated, central data manager component as required by design, but it contains code that performs data-access operations that do not use this data manager.
